$schema: workload-definitions v1 — representative modeled workloads, not observed user behavior
notes: Token targets are anchored to real limits found in the Aether codebase (app/src/agent/AgentKernel.ts, app/src/agent/runner.ts, app/src/webresearch/ResearchEngine.ts, app/src/llm/LiteRtService.ts), not invented. A fixed system-prompt overhead is added to input tokens identically for both the local and cloud side of every workload, so the comparison stays matched.

shared_assumptions.system_prompt_note: Fixed assistant system-prompt overhead, applied equally to local and cloud input token counts for every workload. Not a measured Aether system-prompt length; a conservative round-number placeholder pending direct measurement.
shared_assumptions.http_overhead_note: Fixed allowance for TLS/HTTP request and response framing on the cloud path only. Local inference has no network path and is not charged this overhead.

workloads.label: Short
workloads.description: A brief factual or conversational request — the kind of single-turn exchange that dominates everyday chat.
workloads.anchor: Below AgentKernel.ts PROPOSE_MAX_TOKENS (220); representative of ordinary short chat replies, not that cap itself.

workloads.label: Standard
workloads.description: An ordinary assistant task with a moderate-length response — a paragraph-scale answer or short piece of writing.
workloads.anchor: Between runner.ts default maxTokens (256) and ResearchEngine.ts ANSWER_MAX_TOKENS (640).

workloads.label: Extended
workloads.description: A structured task with a longer response — multi-part writing, comparison, or synthesis.
workloads.anchor: Matches the scale of AgentKernel.ts ARTIFACT_MAX_TOKENS (900) and refine.ts REVISE_MAX_TOKENS (900).

local_configuration.model_label: Gemma 4 E2B (Aether "Fast" mode, the default mode)
local_configuration.prefill_note: No official GPU-backend prefill figure for this exact model/device was found. 500 tok/s is a conservative (slow) placeholder bound versus the 1916 tok/s Pixel 7 Pro CPU-backend prefill figure reported in the same product line; prefill time is a small fraction of total generation time at these workload sizes regardless, since decode dominates wall-clock time. See limitations.md.
local_configuration.reference_device: 8 GB+ RAM Android device meeting Aether's stated minimum (app/src/models/registry.ts minRamGb: 8), Snapdragon 8-series-class SoC, GPU inference delegate active.
local_configuration.device_generalization_note: This is a single reference-class device assumption. Actual on-device throughput and power draw vary by chipset, thermal state, and RAM headroom. Not generalized to all Android phones.

cloud_configuration.label: Cloud-based LLM inference (generic, unnamed service)
cloud_configuration.compute_hardware_class: Data-center GPU serving hardware, single/unbatched request attribution (see limitations.md batching caveat)
cloud_configuration.streaming_rate_note: Assumption, not a cited measurement: the wall-clock pace at which a cloud response is displayed to the user, which determines how long the phone's radio stays active during a streamed reply. Order-of-magnitude consistent with commonly observed streaming-assistant response pacing. Low streaming-rate scenario = high radio energy (worse for cloud); high streaming-rate = low radio energy (better for cloud).

exclusions_for_all_workloads: Software distribution infrastructure beyond the model file / app download itself
Non-AI app usage (navigation, storage browsing, settings)
User screen power (identical for both conditions while reading a reply; excluded from both)
External tools used by optional features (Research web-fetching network cost; Task mode tool calls)
Per-session model load time/energy (amortized differently than per-query cost; out of scope for v1)
Server-side request batching efficiency (see limitations.md — likely makes real-world cloud energy lower than modeled here)
